Run the checks#

This page shows how the project is built, tested and released, and where changes land.

Checks: composer ci (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in MAINTAINING.md.

composer ci is the contract: manifest, tests, Pint, PHPStan, composer audit, and a check that the front page versions table still matches CREED's policy. PHP is not needed on the host:

docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"

(On Windows PowerShell ${PWD} works as written; in Git Bash use $(pwd -W) and set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1.)

The GitLab pipeline (.gitlab-ci.yml) and the GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) both wrap composer ci, on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and the stack's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.

The front page has its own accessibility gate (axe-core in Playwright, run in Docker): scripts/a11y.sh on Linux and macOS, scripts/a11y.ps1 on Windows; MAINTAINING.md says when to run it.

Contributing#

The canonical repository is enterprise-apps/rollcall on git.wayne.edu; changes land there first, and Wayne State developers open issues and merge requests on that project. GitHub (waynestate/rollcall) is a read-only push mirror of git.wayne.edu: nobody pushes to it, and Packagist reads from it.
